_comment: Your resume, broken into reusable pieces. `tags` drive which bullets get suggested for a given posting — edit the tags freely, they are matching hints, not resume text. `text` is what actually goes on the resume, so keep it accurate.
_experience_comment: Order here is the order on the rendered resume (reverse-chronological). `section` decides which heading a role sits under. Bullets are attached by matching `company` + `role`.

projects.title: A project of yours
projects.text: What you built and what it did.

answers._comment: Prose answers for the ATS prep pack. Personal narrative, so it lives here rather than in prep_package.py. {company} is substituted at render time.
answers.why_this_company_opening: One or two sentences on your background and the work you have enjoyed most.
answers.why_leaving: Why you are looking, in your own words.
answers.greatest_strength: A strength, with one concrete result attached.

background._comment: Prompt-ready bios. They name employers and a bank he asks not to be named in drafts, so they live here, not in the prompts themselves -- the repository is public and this file is not.
background.outreach:
- Your degree, school and graduation date.
- Your current role and employer.
- Earlier roles worth mentioning, and how to refer to them.
- Your tools, languages and work authorization.
background.job_search:
- Your degree and school.

- Earlier roles.

evidence.text: a line of your own evidence for quantitative roles
a line of your own evidence for credit roles

background.evidence_fallback: a general line of experience, used when no pattern matches
